_comment: Assets carried over from the v0.1.4 oracle, split by whether v0.2 still ships them byte-identically.
The theme round deliberately changed three page assets and added the site's living-background
renderer, so the old 'every asset matches the oracle' claim is no longer true and must not be
asserted. What remains true is recorded under `unchanged` and still checked digest-for-digest;
each divergence carries the reason it happened, so the difference is evidence rather than drift.

app.js.reason: Every action gated on window.confirm silently did nothing: WKWebView implements no JavaScript dialogs, so confirm() returns false without drawing. That killed create-with-relay, start-public-relay, use-my-own-address, revoke-member and withdraw-standing-consent, leaving the two-Mac join path unreachable with no error. Those five sites now await an in-page <dialog id="ask-dialog">. Disclosure trigger buttons toggle their own <details> panel and keep aria-expanded in step. A claimed pairing card now scrolls into view and focuses its Approve button once: below the fold the action was unreachable without scrolling and returned -25202 to assistive presses, so owners could mint code after code without ever approving one. A failed join now names its real code and a next action beside the field instead of leaving the stale 'membership lapsed' line as the only explanation. After the temporary relay's 30-minute window closes its status keeps the old origin, and the page hid Start public relay whenever an origin was present, so the owner could not open a new relay without restarting the app (v0.1.4 has the same dead end): a stopped relay now counts as not up and its line says to start a new one. A joined Mac whose renewals fail (renewal_error / recovery_error) now says so instead of showing nothing (lane PHY item 3): the line says only what its membership state shows (lane PHY patches 2 and 3, PHY-05): current reads renewal failed, retrying (a single failed pass keeps the live session); retained reads renewal retrying with the saved membership; revoked and stale say the owner ended or replaced this Mac's membership and must add it again; absent says this Mac holds no membership; unknown (the seed answered that it does not recognise this Mac) reads the owner's pick (a), 'The owner’s swarm doesn’t recognise this Mac — ask the owner to add it again' (lane C B11 c, ledger rows 100-101), and any other state says the state is not known yet; only an expired membership gets the instruction to have the owner start the relay again and reconnect this Mac. A joined Mac whose launch-time resume failed (recovery_error recorded and the Mac not running) has nothing renewing, so its line now says it is stopped and to press Start / reconnect once the owner's swarm is reachable, instead of promising that Mycelium keeps retrying (lane B, lane C review C-02). Lane CHATS: the removed one-Mac prompt form's handlers ($('infer-form') submit, $('submit'), $('output')) are gone, and the #inference card is hidden unless the owner's last run failed with the prepare_model fix (then it is shown and #acquisition is scrolled into view once per run, because run.js polls on its own timer and may point at the card while it is still hidden) or the owner's download is running; a joined Mac never shows it. Lane XB patch 2 (REVIEW XB-05, decisions D1/D2): one contained block appended at the end of app.js (between '// ---- Network reach (lane XB patch 2) ----' and '// ---- end network reach ----') builds a 'Network · How the Macs reach each other' card after #demo-target with its own status poll: the owner's per-run choice 'Macs on the same network' (default) / 'Macs on different networks (through the Mycelium relay)' and each Mac's portmapping preference (default off), saved through the packaged /api/network/reach action, plus the active mode and named network errors from status.network_reach; v0.1.4 had no cross-network choice. Lane XB patch 3 (REVIEW XB2-04): the same block shows the live path of each connection to another Mac (status.network_reach.paths: through the Mycelium relay or direct, sampled when status is read) and says portmapping was requested without claiming its outcome. Lane XB patch 3 (REVIEW XB2-07): its wording says what crosses which path: on the same network model and stage traffic stay on the network while the run's control messages still pass through the owner's relay link; across networks the relay sees the Macs' addresses (not the content, encrypted end to end), direct paths are tried (including to addresses the other Mac reports), and a Mac without a usable network gets network advice. Lane XB patch 4 (REVIEW XB3-03): each live path names what it carries (control, model data or stage traffic, from status.network_reach.paths[].channel) and the line reads 'Live paths of this run now' (status lists only the active run's connections). The api crate's oracle copy (crates/api/assets/desktop/app.js) is unchanged.

index.html.reason: Adopts the site's dark Green token set and the background renderer's layout rules; the header mark is 56px with the wordmark block vertically centred, disclosures are real text buttons, and (v0.2 copy) the hero no longer claims the device has 'earned' anything at onboarding: it now reads 'add your first device, and see exactly what it shares—and what stays yours', which drops the single-platform wording for a product that will run on other devices too. Lane CHATS (owner ruling 14 Nov, ledger rows 17 and 106 b: one chat path through the run's route, no one-Mac native chat in the packaged app): the #inference card's one-Mac Prompt box and its 'Run on qualified route' button (inert in v0.1.4 too: app.js only prevented the form's submit) and its output box are removed, the nav link to the card is removed, and the card is hidden by default. It is not removed: its model download is still the owner's model-prepare step (owner-run NOT_PREPARED_MESSAGE, demo_chain.py:132-133, names it, and run.js points at #acquisition for the prepare_model fix), so app.js shows it only for that fix or while that download runs. The api crate's oracle copy (crates/api/assets/desktop/index.html, pinned in crates/api/contracts/assets.json) is unchanged.

style.css.reason: Adopts the site's dark Green token set (ground #010301, ink #e7f2e3, accent #58f56a, art tokens --strand/--glow/--core), Fraunces for h1-h3 via the embedded woff2, and the layout rules the background renderer needs (.page-mycelium, .page-mycelium-field, .mycelium-breath, .hero-art). The header mark is 56px with the wordmark block vertically centred against it, and disclosure buttons are styled as plain text inside the summary.

mycelium-field.js.reason: Was carried verbatim from mycelium_swarm_directory/web. The life layer's 128 px tiles left whole colonies clipped as squares: a tile first painted while its neighbourhood was empty kept `cands = false` for good, so strands that grew into it later were never drawn there and terminated on the tile edge. Candidates are now recomputed until a tile has held a strand and boxes are tested with a 2 px bleed, the hero's page-anchored composite fades in over its own first 200 px (the raster is a rectangle, so it read as a knife-cut under the header), and the life tiles fade their part of that same band. Lane GR (owner: the green circles on the nodes vanish when the growth phase ends): drawHero() passes the fade band's height to the hero's scene.drawIntroCores(x, fade) so the hero can restore its baked node cores in that band (see mycelium-hero.js); the ramp itself is unchanged.

chat.js.reason: Lane CAP (owner ruling 15 Nov): the stage capacity is the model contract's serving context (4,096 then; 2,356 by the owner's ruling of 16 Nov, crates/api/contracts/divergences.json), and a prompt the page accepts (2,000 characters) can be up to 8,000 tokens with the byte-level tokenizer, so the route can refuse it (joined_route_context_exceeds_worker). The chat service names that refusal chat_context_too_long; this script gains its message and appends the context from the chat state's limits.context_tokens instead of showing the route's internal code. The page's own limits are unchanged. Lane CHATPAGE item 2 (REVIEW-laneCHATS-astra CHATS-01): this script is now also the public relay's chat script: node-service's relay chat handler (desktop_host/relay_chat.rs) answers the relay's GET /chat/chat.js with desktop::page::CHAT_JS instead of the api crate's pinned v0.1.4 copy, so a room member's page shows the window's refusal messages, never the raw chat_context_too_long. The relay's chat.html and chat.css stay the api crate's pinned v0.1.4 copies (crates/api/contracts/assets.json, unchanged), whose element ids this script drives.

chat.html.reason: Lane CHATPAGE (owner, 16 Nov 21:58-22:15; brief CHATPAGE-2026-11-16 item 1): "Open the chat on this Mac" navigates the packaged window to mycelium://localhost/chat, and v0.1.4's page there had its own old look and NO way back to the main page, so the owner could reach neither Stop nor Quit from the window (v0.1.4 opened it in a browser tab beside the app; the packaged window pins every link into its one window). The window's chat page now loads the main page's style.css (the app's tokens, the Fraunces face, the header mark) before chat.css, shows a visible 'Back to Mycelium' link to / (a pinned destination) and a 'Stop the run' button wired by the window-only /chat/owner.js. Every element chat.js and the qualification probe drive keeps its v0.1.4 id (state, served, log, form, prompt, tokens, send) and the room notice is unchanged. The public relay never serves this page: it serves the api crate's pinned v0.1.4 chat.html and chat.css, with this crate's chat.js.

chat.css.reason: Lane CHATPAGE item 1: v0.1.4's chat.css declared its own palette (--bg #101b19, --panel #192923, ...) and system fonts, so the window's chat page did not look like the app. It is now only the chat's layout (log bubbles, the prompt row, the owner controls) on the app's tokens from style.css, which the window's chat.html loads first; it declares no :root palette of its own. Window only: the relay's chat page keeps the api crate's pinned v0.1.4 chat.css.

mycelium-hero.js.reason: Was carried verbatim from mycelium_swarm_directory/web (18c88c92850d49093b08f43e949ae4a4348dd5b5844247f6d7a6548c18efa5a6). Lane GR (owner: on first load the nodes have green circles in the growth phase, which disappear after the growth phase finishes): the colony cores (the soft green discs on the nodes) are drawn by scene.drawIntroCores over the composite while they build up, after mycelium-field.js's 200 px top fade ramp, then baked into the hero raster once complete, where that ramp erased up to ~90% of the cores of the nodes near the art's top edge. Once baked, drawIntroCores now adds back the share of the cores the ramp removed (the cores masked by the same ramp, cached in one band canvas), so the nodes keep what the grow-in showed. Visual only: timing, geometry, colours, the ramp and every other layer are unchanged; v0.1.4's page had no hero animation.

mycelium-boot.js.source: app-local: boots createHero/createField, dark Green only (no hue or theme switch)

mark.svg.reason: mycelium colony mark (W2) replacing the inherited asterisk glyph; drawn for both the site and the app

chat-owner.js.source: app-local (lane CHATPAGE item 1): the window chat page's owner controls, served only by the window at /chat/owner.js. 'Stop the run' sends the main page's own Stop request (run.js act('/api/demo/stop', {}): POST, JSON, X-Mycelium-Action: 1) and is shown only to the owner, enabled only while the run is running or serving; the relay never serves this script and refuses an owner action whatever a page sends.

icon.source: authored: W2 colony mark (icons/icon.png regenerated from the chosen mark)
icon.reason: macOS icons carry their own squircle mask; the tile was square and read as a foreign shape in the Dock.
